description: [FREE: 25 calls/day, then $0.01 USDC per call via x402] Give it your rows (JSON or CSV) and the figures you need; it returns them computed exactly (decimal arithmetic, no floating point), so your agent never has to add up a column in its head. Metrics are expressions: sum([Amount]), avg(price), count(), count_distinct([Customer]), median(days), min/max, sum(qty * price), sum(amount) / total(amount) * 100 (share of the overall total), round(x, 2), avg(days_between([Invoiced], [Paid])), sum(age_days([Due])) with asOf. Group by columns or periods: month([Date]), week, quarter, year, weekday, or ranges such as bucket(age_days([Due]), 30, 60, 90) for an aging report. Optional: where filters (numbers or dates), sort, limit. Cells that are not numbers are never counted as 0: they are skipped and reported with row numbers (or refused with strictNumbers). Up to 10000 rows. The same input always gives the same output, with a receipt.

asOf.description: the date age_days() counts up to, YYYY-MM-DD (required for age_days: answers never silently depend on today's date)

csv.description: the data as CSV text with a header row (instead of rows)

dateFormat.description: how to read slash dates like 03/04/2026: mdy (US) or dmy; ISO dates (2026-03-04, with or without a time) are always read. Default iso

groupBy.description: one figure set per distinct value: a column name, or a key such as month([Date]), week([Date]) (ISO), quarter, year, day, weekday, or bucket(age_days([Due]), 30, 60, 90) for ranges

limit.description: return at most this many groups

expr.description: e.g. sum([Amount]) or sum(qty * price) / count()

rounding.description: rounding rule when scale applies; default half_up

rows.description: the data as JSON objects, one per row (up to 10000). Numbers as decimal strings are safest; JSON numbers are accepted

scale.description: decimal places for every figure; default: exact, or 18 places when a value has no finite decimal form (like 1/3)

by.description: a metric name or a groupBy column

strictNumbers.description: true: refuse any cell that is not a plain decimal (no $, commas, %, or text in number columns). Default false: those are read and every change is reported

where.description: keep only rows matching ALL of these: eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte (numeric when both sides are numbers), contains (case-insensitive), in (list), empty, not_empty

value.description: text; a list for "in"; numbers as decimal strings

name: table_calc
title: Exact math over a table (sums, averages, per-group totals) — no hallucinated numbers
